summary: The round-6 blocker is fixed. I probed the base STL: a 7 x 3 mm groove in the underside (x -37.7..-30.7, z 0..3) runs from the widened open pocket (y -22) out past the -Y plate edge. The lead is laid in from below, so the plug never passes a hole, and base_fea shows the groove region cold (hot spots are on the tower and a front bolt foot, p99.9 0.96 MPa against 13). The cable-boss value is now read from the catalog. However, the engine's new perimeter-aware masses made the printed links 15-45 % heavier (arm 791 g, not 693 g). All hand-entered FEA loads still use the old masses, so upper_arm_fea now applies about 1.88x the static elbow load where the brief's contract requires 2x, and the DESIGN.md numbers are stale.

findings.issue: The FEA load cases are no longer 2x the real static loads. After the ENG-6 perimeter-aware mass change, report.json and bom.md give upper_arm 64.8 g (was 47), forearm 55.4 (40), gripper 29.4 (22), finger 5.0 (4), base 175 (134), and arm_mass 791 g (DESIGN says 693). The upper_arm_fea 'why' says 3.87 N is everything beyond the elbow plus 150 g. With the current masses that is el_servo 60 + el_horn 3 + forearm 55.4 + wr_servo 55 + wr_horn 3 + gripper 29.4 + gr_servo 55 + gr_horn 3 + finger 5 + payload 150 = 418.8 g = 4.11 N. 2x is 8.21 N, but 7.74 N is applied. The elbow torque is 2 x 4.46 kg*cm = 875 N*mm (torque_elbow now reports 4.46), but 841 is applied. The brief's grading contract requires upper_arm_fea at '2x the worst static load at the elbow incl. payload', and it currently runs at about 1.88-1.96x. The other hand-entered loads are low by 3-7 % for the same reason: forearm 2.86 N (now 2.95), yoke 5.9 N, turntable/base 12.8 N (about 13.7 now) and the 0.85 N*m tipping moment (the shoulder torque is now 8.21 kg*cm, not 7.80). None of the results would flip, since the margins are large and the stall cases are dominated by the unchanged stall torques. Even so, the checks no longer prove what their 'why' text and the brief say.
findings.fix: Recompute every hand-entered load in project.yaml from the current report masses. Use upper_arm_fea 2 x 4.11 N and 2 x 4.46 kg*cm = 875 N*mm, forearm 2 x 2.95 N and 2 x 1.91 kg*cm, the yoke and turntable weight from the current turntable-borne mass, and the tipping moment from the current shoulder torque. Better still, derive them in layout.py or an expression from the masses so they cannot go stale again. Update the 'why' strings and the DESIGN.md tables to match: the sizing table (shoulder 8.21 = 39 %, elbow 4.46 = 23 %), the hand check, the part-list masses, the 693 g figure and the Strength table. Then rebuild.

findings.issue: Stale cut. The old yaw-lead hole through the gear guard ring is still there: base.py lines 78-80, Box 12 x 6 x 10 at (-45, -31.25, z 6..16). I confirmed it in the STL at x -50..-38, and it is visible in part_base_sheet.png FRONT. Nothing uses it now. It is an open 12 x 10 mm hole into the guard, whose stated job is to keep cable loops out, and its comment describes a route that no longer exists.
findings.fix: Delete the guard-hole cut and its comment so the ring is closed at the bottom.

findings.issue: The yaw lead bends hard at the grommet. The pocket's +X end wall is at x -27.4 (STL), only 0.6 mm past the catalog's 7.0 mm cable-boss envelope (case end -35.0, envelope tip -28.0). The real MG996R wires leave the boss heading +X, so they must turn down against that wall almost at the grommet, and during the push-up from below they drag along it. The route still works because the pocket is open below and the wires are thin, but it is a kink point at the strain relief. Also, nothing holds the lead in the groove while the base is turned over onto the desk.
findings.fix: Give the end wall 2-3 mm more clearance at boss height, or chamfer the wall's lower inside edge. In DESIGN.md step 2, say to pre-bend the lead downward at the boss before pushing the servo up, and to hold the lead in the groove with a strip of tape while turning the base over.

findings.issue: Round-6 route item, only partly fixed. pwr_yaw and sig_yaw now pass base.yaw_boss (-30.4, 0, 13), but the engine still adds the servo origin (-55.2, 0, 27.8) as the last point, so the drawn lead still ends inside the MG996R case (report.json electrical.wires points).
findings.fix: Engine: end a lead at the servo's cable-boss point (a 'lead' joint on the servo proxy) instead of its origin. This is general and would fix every project.

findings.issue: Carried over: the optional 45 degree chamfer under the floor bridge's -X side was not done, so the 6 x 5 mm overhang will sag slightly.
findings.fix: Optional: chamfer the bridge block's -X underside at 45 degrees.

findings.issue: Carried over: kerf/electrical.py still leaves out the ATO fuse's cold resistance (about 45 mV at 2.5 A) and the holder's lead, and the servo entries have no sourced lead gauge. Margin is still positive (worst stall row about 151 mV above 4.8 V; the yaw run shows 5.16 V peak).
findings.fix: Engine: add the fuse cold resistance and the holder lead to each run's loop resistance; add a sourced lead gauge to the servo entries.

findings.issue: Carried over: 12.6 % of the surface prints on support. Cosmetic.
findings.fix: Optional: set the column flush with one long side of the foot so it prints without support.

findings.issue: Carried over and accepted: the Nano, the WAGO splices and the fuse holders sit loose on the desk.
findings.fix: None required; a printed electronics tray on the rear pad would be tidier and short-proof.

findings.issue: For the record: upper_arm_stall_fea p99.9 is 13.42 MPa against 16 MPa (margin 1.19). The peak of 18.76 MPa is at the elbow servo window frame in plate A, on the load path in the render. This is the thinnest margin on the arm. It will drop slightly once the static part of the load is corrected (see the major finding), but the 19 kg*cm stall couple dominates. The DS32xx tab holes are still UNVERIFIED in the catalog.
findings.fix: None required beyond rerunning it after the load update; test-fit the real DS3225/DS3218 before printing the rest.
